resources.string: Shows that the app is connected to the doorbell hub.
Rings when someone presses the doorbell.
Missed rings and new visitor messages.
Not in Wi-Fi. The doorbell only reaches you at home.
The hub does not know this phone any more
The ring at %1$s was answered by %2$s.
Answered. Hold the button to talk.
Someone else is talking at the door
Allow the microphone to talk to the door
The app only works in the home Wi-Fi. You see and hear the door, and hold a button to talk.
Allow notifications, otherwise you will not hear the doorbell.
Allow full-screen notifications, so that a ring shows the door even when the phone is locked.
Let the app run in the background without battery restrictions, so that it stays connected to the hub.
The phone is removed from the hub and no longer rings. You can pair it again at any time.
The phone asks the hub for access. You then approve it in the web interface of the hub.
Looking for the hub in the Wi-Fi …
Address of the hub, e.g. doorbell-hub.home.arpa
Open %1$s in a browser and approve this phone under \"Devices asking for access\". The code there must be the same.
Create a client in the web interface of the hub and enter its token here.
Enter the address of the hub, e.g. doorbell-hub.home.arpa.
The hub cannot be reached. Is the phone in the home Wi-Fi?
The hub answered with an error (HTTP %1$d).
The request has expired. Please ask again.
The hub does not know this phone (any more).
Too many devices are asking at the moment. Try again in a few minutes.
Enter a name with at most 64 characters.
The phone is not in a Wi-Fi.
